items_missed: 1_set_agenda: never asked 'how are you today,' gave no agenda statement (what he'd cover / how long it'd take), and never asked an explicit 'sound good?'

2_probe: didn't address the known doorway/tight-turn problem that caused the sectional piece to get stuck last time, and brushed past the customer calling this move 'a nightmare' with just 'Oh, no' instead of asking what's worrying her

3_pricing: no 'pricing is super simple' opener, didn't cover what's included (insurance, wrap pads, tools), no disassembly/reassembly mention despite the sectional issue, no No Worries Damage Coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, no full no-hidden-fees pitch
4_clock: never explained clock start, the 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute prorated increments, or checked 'does that make sense'
5_estimate: didn't call out the elevator/stairs or the sectional disassembly issue as time variables feeding the 5-hour estimate
6_save_your_ass: entire prep speech skipped — no mention prep shortens the move, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip

7_quote_booking: no 'no deposit required' mention, didn't describe a bolded confirmation list in the email, didn't ask for reply-with-corrections, never asked 'any other questions before I let you go,' and didn't give hours or how to reach the branch
8_politeness: never used the customer's actual name — called her 'sir' twice even after she introduced herself as Mara
9_bonus: no rapport or humor moment, no insurance explanation (No Worries + 60c/lb), no proactive FAQ coverage
top_strength: Jules moved fast and stayed organized on a genuinely multi-part job — pulling up the prior move file, confirming the exact unit number ('I wanna make sure the condo in Central Avenue is unit 4104'), and tracking three separate legs (warehouse pickup, condo delivery, sectional piece returning to the warehouse) without dropping a detail, all in under six minutes.
coaching_note: You got the logistics right but lost the person. You called her 'sir' twice after she told you her name was Mara — slow down and actually use the customer's name. You also skipped almost every differentiator: no prep speech, no clock explanation, no damage coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee. This was a quick add-on booking, but that's exactly when reps get lazy on the pitch — run the framework every time, not just on first-time full quotes.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and responsive throughout, but calling the customer 'sir' twice despite her introducing herself as Mara shows he wasn't tracking who he was talking to, which flattens the rapport.
